title: 1 · Where the corpus is now
description: What the pipeline holds right now, counted off the tables that hold it. The logs say what happened once; these say what is true. A row a worker died holding logged nothing and is still counted here, which is the difference that matters when something has gone quiet.

options.content:
**What this answers:** how far every stage has got, and what it refused. Counted off the tables, so a row a dead worker was holding is still counted here.

**Grafana's job is state and logs.** For the *calls* behind a step go to **Phoenix**; for *which run* produced it, **Dagster**; for *what a person said about it*, **Argilla**; for *how one artefact was produced*, the "How this was produced" fold on the application's own pages.

panels.title: Queue depth by stage
panels.description: Every stage's queue in one shape. `new` is a row nobody has asked for yet and is not waiting on a worker - it is waiting on a person. `pending` is claimable and is the only thing a worker takes. A pending column that does not fall is a stage with no worker behind it, which reads exactly like a broken one.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT stage, status, rows FROM (
  SELECT 1 AS ord, 'parsing'  AS stage, parse_status   AS status, count(*) AS rows FROM documents GROUP BY parse_status
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 2, 'chunking',   chunk_status,   count(*) FROM documents GROUP BY chunk_status
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 3, 'extraction', extract_status, count(*) FROM passages  GROUP BY extract_status
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 4, 'topics',     status,         count(*) FROM topics WHERE topic_index IS NULL GROUP BY status
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 5, 'questions',  question_status, count(*) FROM topics WHERE topic_index IS NOT NULL GROUP BY question_status
) q ORDER BY ord, status

panels.title: Failed, by stage
panels.description: A failed row is recoverable and stays where it is until something returns it: `retry` on that stage, or the Retry button beside it. Nothing sweeps them up on its own, so a number here that never moves is a number nobody has looked at.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 'parsing' AS stage, count(*) AS failed FROM documents WHERE parse_status = 'failed'
UNION ALL SELECT 'chunking',   count(*) FROM documents WHERE chunk_status   = 'failed'
UNION ALL SELECT 'extraction', count(*) FROM passages  WHERE extract_status = 'failed'
UNION ALL SELECT 'topics',     count(*) FROM topics WHERE topic_index IS NULL     AND status          = 'failed'
UNION ALL SELECT 'questions',  count(*) FROM topics WHERE topic_index IS NOT NULL AND question_status = 'failed'

panels.title: Why a fact was refused
panels.description: Grouped on the stored code rather than on the English beside it, because the message carries a measurement and would make one bucket per fact. A shift in the mix between runs is the checker or the model changing its mind, and is worth more than the overall rate.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT rejection_code AS reason, count(*) AS facts
FROM facts WHERE rejection_code IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY rejection_code ORDER BY count(*) DESC

panels.title: Facts held, by kind
panels.description: Extraction reads a passage four ways. The share of each is what EXTRACTION_KINDS and the atomic cap were set to control, so this is the panel that says whether they did.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT kind,
       count(*)                                   AS facts,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE validated)          AS accepted,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE validated) / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS "accepted %"
FROM facts GROUP BY kind ORDER BY count(*) DESC

panels.title: Questions, and the gate that refused them
panels.description: A rejected question keeps its row: the share thrown away is the evidence behind the coverage report, and a deleted row is a drop nobody can count. `draft` is written and not yet decided.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT status,
       coalesce(rejected_reason, '-') AS gate,
       count(*) AS questions
FROM questions
GROUP BY status, rejected_reason
ORDER BY count(*) DESC

panels.title: Topics, and how much of the corpus each holds
panels.description: One model per language over that language's passages only. A topic nobody put in coverage is written no questions at all, which is a decision and not a gap - `include_in_coverage` says which.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT t.language,
       t.topic_index                  AS topic,
       coalesce(t.label, '(unnamed)') AS label,
       t.labelled_by,
       t.include_in_coverage          AS in_coverage,
       count(DISTINCT pt.passage_id)  AS passages,
       t.question_status
FROM topics t
LEFT JOIN passage_topics pt ON pt.topic_id = t.id
WHERE t.topic_index IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY t.id, t.language, t.topic_index, t.label, t.labelled_by,
         t.include_in_coverage, t.question_status
ORDER BY t.language, t.topic_index
